speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To begin our assessment, have you ever experienced any sudden, severe headache or double vision during these dizzy spells?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. To narrow down the cause, does the spinning sensation last only seconds when you change your head position, or does it persist for minutes? Also, have you noticed any new hearing loss, ringing in the ears, or a feeling of fullness in your affected ear?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The history of short-lived, position-dependent spinning without other neurological deficits is classic for this condition. Please perform the Dix-Hallpike maneuver at your next visit to confirm the diagnosis and identify the affected canal.
